Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme DPA redlines (initial) — privacy review (round 1)

Mike / Rachel —

I reviewed Acme's redlines and summarized below. See attached RI_privacy_comments_round1.pdf for line-by-line notes. High-level positions:

1) Subprocessors / Notice Window
- Acme asks for 30 days. Our standard is 30 days for notice and 15 days for objection; for sensitive subprocessors (security monitoring, hosting) we typically provide 30 days and accommodate reasonable objections. Recommend accepting 30 days notice but keep objection process as-written.

2) EU->US Transfers / SCCs
- We can accept SCCs as the legal basis for transfers. Acme's proposed Art 46 fallback language is broader than necessary; recommend we propose the standard SCCs + a supplemental transfer addendum limited to the contract term. Avoid open-ended Art 46 language.

3) Liability caps / Carve-outs
- Acme proposes a carve-out for regulatory penalties. We should not accept uncapped exposure. Suggest a limited carve-out tied to gross negligence or willful misconduct, with an overall negotiated cap.

4) Evidence & Audit
- SOC 2 Type II: we can share an executive summary and a time-limited evidence bundle via secure link. Naomi, please confirm which artifacts are ok to share and the Drive link.

5) Execution path (eSign)
- Recommend DocuSign route for speed. I can prepare a redline-friendly DPA with inline comments and a proposed compromise on subprocessor notice/objection. If Acme insists on countersignature by counsel via DocuSign, that's fine — we'll route to Legal Ops to track.

Next steps:
- Naomi: confirm shareable evidence + generate link.
- Rachel: please re-engage Jordan to propose a 48-hour window for follow-up and confirm whether Acme will accept SCCs + addendum rather than Art 46 fallback language.
- I'll prepare an internal redline (legal position) and a suggested message for Mike to send to the customer.

Monica
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI_privacy_comments_round1.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Acme DPA redlines (initial) — proposed compromise + eSign link

Jordan —

Thanks for the redlines and for pulling your counsel in. We reviewed and propose the following compromise to unblock procurement quickly:

- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide 30-days' notice for new subprocessors. Acme will have a 15-day objection window; if Acme raises a reasonable objection, Redwood will engage to either offer a mitigation or postpone onboarding.
- Transfers: Redwood accepts SCCs + a short transfer addendum limited to the term; we will not agree to open-ended Art 46 fallback language.
- Liability carve-out: Redwood will accept a narrowly tailored carve-out tied to gross negligence / willful misconduct, subject to a reciprocal cap (proposed text attached).

We have prepared an internal clean DPA with these positions and a redline copy for reference. To accelerate execution we've started an envelope in DocuSign. Please review the DocuSign envelope and sign if the compromise is acceptable: https://docusign.net/Envelope/1234abcdef

If Acme prefers a short call (15 minutes) to confirm the compromise before eSign, Rachel and I are available today between 2–4pm PT. Otherwise, if we get a signed DPA via DocuSign we will route countersignature from our side immediately.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Clean_vACME_2026.docx (docx, 56 KB), Redwood_DPA_Redline_vACME_2026.pdf (pdf, 24 KB)
